[TTB] Why this generation is interesting
The big changes are OLED, optional nano-texture glass, A20 Pro, lower weight, thinner design, IP67 water resistance and Wi-Fi 7 .
For someone who already has a phone, the new mini also becomes an interesting alternative to paying $3,499+ for an iPhone Duo just to get a larger portable OLED display.

The iPhone Duo obviously remains a phone and has the superior 120Hz display, brightness and cameras . But the mini gives you a larger 8.5-inch OLED display for roughly one-third of the Australian Duo price , making it an interesting companion to an existing phone.
The optional nano-texture display also gives the mini something the previous generation did not offer.
The biggest compromise is that Apple has kept the iPad mini at 60Hz despite moving to OLED.
I haven't included the M-series iPad Air because the smallest Air is 11 inches, putting it in a materially different size class from the mini / foldable-phone use case.
[Orrelljet] I think your maths is a little flawed. In order to make a proper comparison, you need to even out the specs. A 512GB wifi/cellular IPad Mini OLED with nano texture glass costs $1929 from the Education store and a 512GB iphone Duo $3899 so it’s’ closer to half. Still a great saving but not to the extent you’re suggesting and you’re still stuck with a 60Hz display.
